survey: A stack of three folded paper maps lying flat, seen from above and in front, turned about 30° so the front edge runs down to the left. The top sheet is a flat parallelogram. Its left and right edges and its fold that runs front to back are all parallel (blue, about 57°). Its front edge, back edge and fold that runs side to side are also parallel (red, about 166°). The front edge of each sheet rolls under into a soft tube, and the open ends of the tubes face the viewer at the front left. The two lower sheets are the same shape, each shifted a little down and to the right. Their side edges stay parallel to the top sheet's edges, and their front-to-back folds run on from the top sheet's fold in the same direction. The printed path, lakes and X lie flat on the paper and shrink with it. The small mountain icons are flat symbols printed on the map. The stack has no visible ground, but the overlaps show each sheet resting on the one below at the same angle. One camera covers the whole stack, and the slight lack of convergence is mild stylized near-isometric drawing.
